newsitem.title: UK: Wace shares plunge after profits warning.
newsitem.headline: Wace shares plunge after profits warning.

text.p: Shares in imaging and printing specialist Wace Group Plc plunged on Thursday after it warned that its 1996 profits would be "substantially lower than current market expectations."
The group's shares were down 45 percent, or 61-1/2 pence, to 75 pence by 1601 GMT, after touching a low of 70 pence.
Analysts said investors's patience with the company had worn out after a series of warnings and remedial actions failed to turn Wace around.
The company said its performance in September and October had fallen "considerably below management's expectations."
Wace announced plans for a series of closures and disposals and said it intended to focus on its higher margin businesses.
Henderson Crosthwaite analyst Louise Barton said she expected the group to post a loss this year, but to start to recover in 1997.
"They are not going to go under. They will find their way out of this," she said, adding that she thought Wace "is clearing the decks dramatically."
